title: Pseudo-coherence of open restrictions of a relatively flat proper image
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, and $F$ a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $f$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Supply independent derived localizations on $X$ and $S$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For any open $U\subseteq S$, supply a derived localization on $U$ in the target morphism universe and localizations on its open sites. The exact open restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] of $Rf_*(F[0])$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] to $U$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No finite Tor interval, lower bound on a representative or perfectness is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A1H (perfect-lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect), Noetherian approximation paragraph specialized to the single module; Tags 08E2, 08E8 and 08E7

proof.text: Work locally on an affine neighbourhood inside the given open U. Regard F as the complex in degree zero and the structure sheaf as the tensor unit. Apply Noetherian approximation of tensor data: finite presentation, relative flatness and proper support descend to a Noetherian stage. The unit has a rank-one strictly perfect representative; properness of f gives proper support of the single module.

At the Noetherian stage, finitely presented terms are coherent. The descended perfect object tensored with the descended bounded complex has bounded coherent cohomology, whose support is contained in the finite union of the descended proper term supports. Apply bounded coherent proper-support direct image and then the Noetherian bounded-coherent pseudo-coherent criterion. Thus the stage direct image is pseudo-coherent. Neither finite Tor dimension of the image nor perfection of the image is invoked.

Use relatively flat derived base change to identify the pulled stage direct image with the single-module image on the original affine neighbourhood. Pull a bounded-above finite-free representative back termwise; bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat, so this computes derived pullback and keeps the finite ranks and upper bound. Exact open restriction identifies this object with the restriction to U. Uniqueness of localization compares the Q-images of the same complexes; the K-injective factorization computes both direct images using the same resolution. Transport through the exact localized-site equivalences. These representatives satisfy the local definition of pseudo-coherence. For the empty open the assertion is vacuous, and for the zero module use zero representatives.

lean.statement:
theorem properFlat_single_open_isPseudoCoherent
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace))]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hF : F.IsFlatOver f) (U : S.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : U.toScheme.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace).over V))] :
    U.toScheme.IsPseudoCoherent ((schemeOpenRestriction S U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F)))
